text: Not as described. I was very hopeful these tapes would be exactly what I needed, but they were not. They are described as being 1/2 inch (.5") wide rolls, but as shown in the pictures I included, they are well below this - measuring a little under 3/8 inch, or between 8-9mm. Additionally, these tapes have a glossy finish, unlike many other highlighter tapes, which are usually matte and able to be written on. The tapes are also very light, again as seen in the photo provided. While a very subtle highlight might work for some, I was hoping for a brighter, more easy to spot color. Finally, while not tested long-term, I am not certain these can truly be considered removable. They proved difficult to peel after applying to standard paper, and seemed to be leaving some residue behind. It also seems that the tape color is part of the adhesive, rather than the plastic of the tape. Overall, these tapes are not horrible, which I why I gave three stars. You do get a large quantity of tape for the price. They could very well serve someone's needs well, if matched to the tape's characteristics. For my needs, they are too narrow, too pale and not writable. They are not as described in the product listing, so I am returning this product. Edit: These tapes are definitely NOT removable. (See fourth image.) After sitting on the paper for a couple hours, the tape tore the surface of the paper and removed the type when I attempted to peel it off. Deducted a star from my original review, because I find this to be quite problematic. Again, definitely not as described.

text: Not for beginners, but the print quality is AMAZING. 3D printing is a hobby in and of itself, and resin printers are no different. I had a filament printer in the past, and it was fairly easy to use, but the visible layers always bothered me. Then I found out that resin printers dropped in price. I got one immediately. there is a bit more work to do on the prints: post print cleaning and curing. but it's well worth the extra couple of steps. the quality is AMAZING. there are a few more tools that you need, the only things you will NEED before you start printing is something to wash the prints in like a tub or something, isopropyl alcohol for the wash (other less expensive solutions exist - DO SOME RESEARCH), and something like a tray to cure the prints on in the sun (or you could get your own UV light - I made my own cure chamber using printed parts, a UV lamp and spinning turntable) There are PLENTY of videos on YouTube with directions, hints, warnings and the like - PLEASE watch a LOT of them, they really help. after that, you will be printing the BEST quality objects with little effort.
